title: Contextual fingerprint gating for canary rollouts
creator: Marcus Li
description:
Problem: Current canary/A-B rollouts rely on aggregate score deltas from golden prompt sets which can be noisy for short-lived canaries and fail to capture contextual regressions that depend on prompt shape or customer cohort. We need a lightweight per-prompt "fingerprint" gating layer that detects shifts in response characteristics (semantic embedding drift, length/profile changes, hallucination signals) and ties those signals to rollout decisioning without requiring full manual review for every small regression.

Proposed design: Build a Contextual Fingerprint Gating service that: 
- Ingests canary and baseline responses for a configurable probe set (golden + contextual probes).
- Computes multiple compact fingerprints per prompt: embedding centroid distance, token-length distribution delta, top-k token entropy delta, and a lightweight hallucination heuristic (presence of unexpected entity types).
- Aggregates per-prompt fingerprints into per-cohort risk scores using configurable weightings and a short-term baseline window (rolling 1h/6h).
- Exposes a gating decision API that returns: pass | warn | quarantine with reasoning and top contributing prompts.
- Integrates with rollout conductor: canary flips are blocked on quarantine; warn surfaces to SRE/PM slack channel and to rollout dashboard with suggested mitigation (reduce traffic, revert model, run targeted eval).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Gate computes and stores fingerprints for a 1000-probe set under baseline at ≤ 500ms per request batch in non-prod.
2) Gate rules detect injected regressions in synthetic test (semantic swap + hallucination injection) with >90% recall and <5% false-positive rate on baseline traffic.
3) Gate API returns human-readable top-3 contributing prompts and the fingerprint deltas for auditing.
4) Canary conductor blocks automated promotion when a quarantine is returned and logs a reproducible report to the rollout dashboard.

Trade-offs considered: 
- Full semantic diff via human eval is highest quality but too slow for automated gating; fingerprinting sacrifices some nuance for speed and explainability.
- Embedding-based signals are model-dependent; we mitigate by using model-agnostic token/entropy heuristics and by keeping thresholds per-model/per-customer.

Rollout plan: 
Phase 1 (dev): prototype service + unit tests, local integration with simulated canary traffic (2 weeks).
Phase 2 (staging): instrument canary conductor to call gate in warn mode (no automatic blocks) for 2 weeks and gather metrics.
Phase 3 (progressive): enable quarantine block for low-risk customers and internal canaries, expand to all customers after 4 weeks of stable metrics.

Monitoring & dashboards: rollout dashboard with pass/warn/quarantine counts, per-prompt fingerprint histograms, cohort risk heatmap, and an SLO for false-positive rate on a held-out baseline set.

Security/compliance notes: fingerprints contain no raw customer prompt text in long-term storage; only hashed prompt IDs and aggregated metrics retained.
